Building and editing the tutorials of a package

Source: R/build_tutorials.R
tutorials.Rd

build_tutorials() rebuilds every learnr tutorial in inst/tutorials/ of the package that you work in, for example {manynet}, {autograph}, or {netrics}. For each tutorial it builds:

  • the prerendered HTML file that learnr serves, next to the source .Rmd, and the folder of figures that this file links to, if the tutorial draws any

  • a static article in vignettes/articles/ for the pkgdown website

The articles are a preview of the tutorial and not a replacement for it. The transform shows the demonstration code but does not run it, drops blank exercise chunks and their hints and solutions, and replaces each quiz with a callout that points back to run_tute(). The only chunks it runs are those with a label that starts with explain-. These chunks draw the figures that explain the text, so the article shows their output and hides their code.

edit_tutorial() opens in RStudio the learnr tutorial in inst/tutorials/ of the package in the working directory whose name is nearest to tute.

Usage

build_tutorials(path = ".", tutorials = NULL, html = TRUE, articles = TRUE)

edit_tutorial(tute)

Arguments

path

Path to the root of the package. By default this is the working directory.

tutorials

A character vector that selects the tutorials to build. Each element matches the tutorial folder name or the file name, for example "netrics1" or "centrality". By default all the tutorials are built.

html

Logical. By default TRUE, which rebuilds the prerendered HTML of each tutorial. Set this to FALSE to build the articles only.

articles

Logical. By default TRUE, which rebuilds the static article of each tutorial. Set this to FALSE to build the HTML only.

tute

The name of a tutorial, or of its folder. A name that starts with "tut" is matched to the folder names, and any other name to the file names.

Value

build_tutorials() returns a character vector of the paths of the files and figure folders that are built, returned invisibly.

edit_tutorial() returns the path to the tutorial, invisibly.

Details

The name of the article file comes from the article in vignettes/articles/ that already holds the title of the tutorial. If there is no such article, the name comes from the title itself. For example the title "Making Network Data" gives vignettes/articles/making-network-data.Rmd.

A tutorial that draws figures outside its exercises, such as in the explain- chunks, links to them in a <tutorial>_files/ folder next to the HTML file. The tutorial does not show these figures without the folder, so commit the folder together with the HTML file. Do not embed such figures in the HTML file as base64 data: learnr replaces an image with a video player where the data of the image contains the text "v/".

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
build_tutorials()
build_tutorials(tutorials = "centrality", html = FALSE)
edit_tutorial("centrality")
} # }
